function: Pre-trained ViT foundation model fine-tuned for uplink MIMO-OFDM channel estimation from pilots; also positioning, activity sensing, and RF signal classification, which are outside the areas (p. 1, 9-10).
system: Channel estimation task: single-antenna user, 16-antenna base station, uplink MIMO-OFDM, 14 symbols with pilots at symbols 2 and 11, 3.5 GHz, 30 kHz spacing, 3 m/s (p. 9).
method: Self-supervised masked-autoencoder ViT pre-training (75% masking), then fine-tuning of last 2 of 12 blocks plus a ViT-block head, supervised SNR-weighted MSE; LoRA tested on RF classification (p. 4-7, 10-11).
data_channel: Channel estimation data: Sionna simulation with 3GPP UMi. Pre-training on measured RF spectrograms (3,332), WiFi CSI (840), and 5G CSI (476) samples (p. 8-9).
test_conditions: Pre-train on measured RF, WiFi, 5G data (800 epochs); fine-tune and test on Sionna UMi data with 80%-20% split, SNR -10 to 20 dB (p. 9-11).
baselines: Non-learned LS and LMMSE; learned ViT-SL (same ViT trained from scratch) and ViT variants pre-trained on RF-S, WiFi-CSI, 5G-CSI, or RF-S/WiFi data (p. 10-12).
metrics: Channel estimation MSE versus SNR and averaged (ViT-All 0.329, ViT-SL 0.405); fine-tuning epochs; accuracy and positioning error for other tasks (p. 11-12).
complexity: Backbone 38.1 M parameters, 14.93 GFLOPs per sample, 145.2 MB weights, expected 25 ms on Jetson Orin Nano; 1.5 M parameters per task head (p. 15).
openness: none by the authors; uses public 5G-CSI (DOI 10.21227/k2f0k132) and CommRad RF (Zenodo) datasets (p. 16).
q1_support: p. 9: "We employ the Urban Microcell (UMi) channel model specified by 3GPP" - channel-estimation data simulated with Sionna [30]; the paper does not name TR 38.901, but the Sionna UMi model is the TR 38.901 one; the pre-training CSI is also measured.
q2_support: p. 11: "unfreeze the last 2 of the 12 ViT blocks and fine-tune them alongside the task head" - the backbone pre-trained on RF-S, WiFi-CSI, and 5G-CSI is adapted to the new Sionna channel-estimation dataset (p. 9); pre-training sets are compared on p. 12.
q3_support: p. 10: "training from scratch with a model of identical size and capacity to the WFM" - LS and LMMSE are non-learned baselines (p. 11), but the only learned baseline ViT-SL is the same architecture without pre-training, a variant of the proposed method; no earlier learned estimator is compared.
q4_support: p. 15: "A single forward pass costs 14.9 GFLOPs" - Table 5 also gives 38.1 M backbone parameters and 145.2 MB weights; the cost is for the shared backbone, not the channel-estimation head alone.
q5_support: p. 8: "CSI measurements collected with commercial off-the-shelf 5G equipment" - measured 5G CSI from public dataset [26] (IEEE Dataport DOI 10.21227/k2f0k132, p. 16), also CommRad RF on Zenodo (p. 16); the channel-estimation data are Sionna-simulated and no own code or data link is given.
notes: Included for its MIMO-OFDM channel-estimation task (area 2); the other three downstream tasks (human activity sensing, RF signal classification, 5G NR positioning) are outside the seven areas and were not graded. Borderline q1: the paper says UMi is specified by 3GPP via Sionna without naming TR 38.901; reviewer to confirm. Borderline q2: rests on transfer from the pre-training datasets to the simulated channel-estimation set, not on a test with unseen channel conditions. Borderline q5: public measured datasets are used for pre-training and for the other tasks, while the channel-estimation data are generated with Sionna and not released.
